items.title: Carney government amends controversial bill to fast-track pipelines and mines
The U.S. has officially lost its measles elimination status
items.summary_auto: After a deadly year for measles outbreaks, the U.S. has officially lost its measles elimination status, more than a quarter of a century after it first achieved the distinction. The news comes after Canada lost its measles elimination status last November, a distinction it had held for 28 years.

items.title: Stolen 120-year-old church bell found discarded in rural Manitoba ditch
items.summary_auto: A heavy church bell stolen from the top of a belfry in rural Manitoba has been found abandoned in a ditch.

items.title: TC Energy plans Alberta pipeline expansion to serve natural gas demand
items.summary_auto: TC Energy Corp. is looking to seize on booming natural gas demand in Alberta, announcing plans Monday to expand its pipeline network to add an initial billion cubic feet per day of new capacity.

items.title: South Korea to check student collars, eyeglasses at university entrance exams after cheating admission
items.summary_auto: South Korea will tighten checks on students taking the high-stakes national university entrance exam this week, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said, after a candidate in another test confessed to using a hidden ​camera and AI to cheat.

items.title: Tiger Woods returning to competition for first time since car crash and DUI arrest
items.summary_auto: Tiger Woods is returning to competition for the first time in two years, announcing Tuesday he will be playing in the Hero World Challenge at the unofficial event he hosts in the Bahamas.

items.title: Telus abandons involvement in 2 Vancouver AI data centres
items.summary_auto: Telus says it's decided not to proceed with co-developing two Vancouver data centres, and will instead turn its focus to expanding an existing data centre in Kamloops, B.C.

items.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang signals willingness to return as CEO
items.summary_auto: The former CEO of the top AI chipmaker who resigned last week amid a spying scandal said he "would be honoured" ‌to come back as CEO if the board decided his return would be in the best interest of shareholders and employees. Jensen Huang's first public statement since he resigned last week comes as the former leader agreed to answer questions from U.S. lawmakers next month, and as Nvidia's board formed a committee to address export and security concerns.

items.title: Iran fires drones at U.S. base in Bahrain, denies reports of planned dirty bomb attack in D.C.
items.summary_auto: Iran fired drones at a U.S. military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday, even as talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar to end the nearly nine-month war were taking place.

items.title: Canada advances to CONCACAF Nations League semifinals with win over Guatemala
items.summary_auto: The Canadian men's soccer team closed out its 2026 schedule in style on Monday night with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Guatemala to secure a berth in the final four of the CONCACAF Nations League.

items.title: Canadian home sales edged up in October amid overall flat housing market: CREA
items.summary_auto: Home sales across Canada edged up slightly in October — defying the expectations of some analysts — but remained below levels from October 2025, according to the Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA).

items.title: Manitoba real estate trust hopes to use new federal money to address homelessness
items.summary_auto: A real estate investment trust says the funding model it's used to build dozens of affordable units this past year could be replicated to help the federal government address homelessness in Manitoba.

items.title: 5 European countries want to start deporting migrants to Rwanda, despite concerns from human rights groups
items.summary_auto: Five European countries have embarked on a deal with Rwanda to take in migrants whose asylum claims have been rejected. They are hoping the scheme acts as a deterrent, but a similar plan in Britain was quashed after the court called it unlawful.

items.title: Jury in coroner's inquest hears how woman from Alberta died in northwestern Ontario
items.summary_auto: The first day of a coroner's inquest into the death of a woman at Lake of the Woods District Hospital in Kenora, Ont., took place via video conference on Monday. Here's what members of the jury heard about the late Kaylee Martha Dallas Crowchild of Tsuut’ina Nation in southern Alberta and how she ended up in northwestern Ontario.

items.title: Hooked by design: How gambling apps keep 'losers' spending more cash
items.summary_auto: A CBC News investigation has found online gamblers are targets of a sophisticated, multibillion-dollar industry that routinely uses automated inducements and app design features that try to keep heavy users hooked.

items.title: Investigate Trump or work with him? Democrats debate best path forward
items.summary_auto: Still giddy from their sweeping midterm victory, the Democrats now face a dilemma over what to do next. Some factions within the party are urging a strong push to investigate U.S. President Donald Trump, his family and his allies over allegations of corruption. Others insist the Democrats must stay laser-focused on the cost of living.

items.title: P.E.I. author Nicholas Herring wins 2026 Giller Prize for Your Breath in Charcoal
items.summary_auto: Herring is honoured for his novel about two blue-collar islanders in the late ’90s.

items.title: Hundreds of Rocky Balboas break Guinness World Record  | The Moment
items.summary_auto: Mason Lemme tells The National about the moment he was among the 570 people to break the Guinness World Record for the most people dressed as Sylvester Stallone's character Rocky Balboa, at the steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski testifies about escape attempt during alleged kidnapping
items.summary_auto: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski described how he tried to escape and how his alleged kidnappers ultimately released him during his continued testimony at their jury trial in Toronto on Monday.

items.title: Volunteers back in Manitoba after grounding of U.S. flights set them on long road trip home
items.summary_auto: A group of Manitobans doing volunteer work are back home after Friday's closure of U.S. airspace forced them on a long journey across that country.

items.title: Meta would 'consider' pulling services from Canada if lawful access bill passes as is
items.summary_auto: Representatives from Meta say the social media company would have to "consider" pulling encryption services from Canada if the government's proposed lawful access bill passes without further changes.

items.title: The battle for Trump's 'Trash Island' golf course | About That
items.summary_auto: Andrew Chang explains the fight over what U.S. President Donald Trump calls 'Trash Island' — and why a federal judge blocked the Trump administration from closing Washington's historic East Potomac Park. items.title: Data centres in the U.S. put out more carbon emissions in a year than Denmark, says Harvard study
items.summary_auto: The 400 largest data centres in the United States put more heat-trapping gases into the atmosphere in one year than the entire nation of Denmark did, and that was before the artificial intelligence boom really got going, according to a Harvard University study published Monday.

items.title: Father calls for apology after son target of racist taunts at Kitchener, Ont., hockey tournament
items.summary_auto: The father of a 16-year-old hockey player says he wants a public apology and cultural-competency training for the league after his son was the target of racist taunts at a tournament in Kitchener, Ont., on Nov. 8.

items.title: The U.K. is granting pardons to women convicted for having abortions
items.summary_auto: The U.K. government says it will grant automatic pardons to all women convicted of having illegal abortions over the last 165 years.

items.title: United Airlines says issue affecting departing flights has been resolved
items.summary_auto: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.

items.title: These 3 friends canoed 8,000 km across Canada: Hear why they did it
items.summary_auto: Nolan Aziz and Will Vyse are part of a trio that canoed from Tadoussac, Que., to a Vancouver beach, portaging when they couldn't paddle. Aziz and Vyse describe their trip, which raised $130,000 for True North Aid, a charity that helps northern and remote Indigenous communities.

items.title: Survivor of fatal boat crash near Squamish speaks out
items.summary_auto: Spencer Seabrooke, a survivor of a fatal boat crash near Squamish, B.C., on Thursday, is speaking out about his experience. Three people died in the crash.

items.title: Journalists call for justice after reporter found dead in Mexican coastal city of Acapulco
items.summary_auto: A Mexican journalist was found dead on Saturday on the outskirts of Acapulco, a popular resort city in the southern Guerrero state, marking the latest in a string of alleged attacks targeting reporters in the country.

items.title: N.L. premier waiting to hear from Quebec on Churchill River power deal
items.summary_auto: Quebec Energy Minister Stéphane Paquet said the Churchill River power deal is not set in stone, setting off a series of questions for Premier Tony Wakeham in Newfoundland and Labrador's House of Assembly.

items.title: Gordie Howe bridge surpasses 1M vehicle crossings while other bridges, tunnel lose traffic
items.summary_auto: The Gordie Howe International Bridge has seen more than a million crossings since it officially opened to vehicle traffic on July 27, according to new numbers from the Bridge and Tunnel Operators Association.

items.title: Parents are skipping vitamin K shots for newborns
items.summary_auto: More parents are skipping vitamin K shots for newborns, but skipping it could lead to dangerous brain bleeds.

items.title: Alberta has tabled a bill for new riding maps. What could a court challenge mean?
items.summary_auto: Alberta’s controversial new riding map is one step closer to implementation after Justice Minister Mickey Amery tabled a bill in the legislature on Monday. But legal experts say a potential court challenge could introduce a high level of uncertainty in advance of the next provincial election.

items.title: Exodus in Poilievre's office as 5 staffers plan departures
items.summary_auto: Five members of the Opposition leader's office have informed Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre they plan to quit. The departures will leave big gaps in Poilievre's office, particularly in communications and policy.

items.title: U.S. Supreme Court set to hear 3 major Trump agenda immigration cases
items.summary_auto: The U.S. Supreme Court made at least two significant rulings to shape immigration policy last year. In the coming months, there will at least three more opinions that could be impactful, as U.S. President Donald Trump's administration seeks to reinterpret a number of laws concerning asylum, deportations and the detention of unauthorized persons in the U.S.

items.title: Carney arrives in China for meeting with Xi Jinping, Asia-Pacific summit
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in China on Monday, where he is set to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and leaders from across the Pacific Rim.

items.title: U.S. captures third women's world hockey title in 4 years, downing rival Canadians
items.summary_auto: Hilary Knight and Kelly Pannek each scored twice as the United States defended its women's world hockey title with a 6-2 win over Canada in Monday's gold-medal game in Herning, Denmark.

items.title: 'I have been found guilty': French actor Gérard Depardieu withdraws appeal of sexual assault conviction
items.summary_auto: French actor Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal of a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set, saying in a statement Monday that he would accept his 18-month suspended sentence.
